$comment: Agent notes for bot settings: commands, menu button, bot profile, callback answers. Shape and rules: scripts/api_notes.py. Every pitfall carries its source label; API means the catalog text quoted in cite.

getMe.purpose: Test the bot's token and read the bot's own profile and switches as BotFullInfo.
use_when: a start-up check that the token works
reading back what setMySettings wrote (privacy mode, topics, inline mode)
avoid_when: per update or per message: read it once at start and cache it

pitfalls.text: Returns BotFullInfo, not User.
pitfalls.cite: getMe: Returns information about the bot in form of a BotFullInfo object.

pitfalls.text: Three settings can't be read back: inline_feedback_share_denominator, can_communicate_with_bots, callback_query_mode.
pitfalls.cite: BotFullInfo fields: none for these three settings

pitfalls.text: Typed SDKs written before 10.5 may still model the result as User and drop fields; read the raw result.

logOut.purpose: Log the bot out of the cloud Bot API server before running it on a local Bot API server.
use_when: moving the bot to a self-hosted Bot API server
avoid_when: a restart or redeploy that stays on the cloud server

pitfalls.text: After success the bot can't log back in to the cloud server for 10 minutes.
pitfalls.cite: logOut: will not be able to log in back to the cloud Bot API server for 10 minutes

pitfalls.text: Log out before running locally, or updates may be missed.
pitfalls.cite: logOut: otherwise there is no guarantee that the bot will receive updates

pitfalls.text: A one-off migration step, not part of start-up code.

close.purpose: Close the bot instance before moving it from one local Bot API server to another.
use_when: migrating a bot between self-hosted Bot API servers
avoid_when: leaving the cloud server: that is logOut

pitfalls.text: Delete the webhook first, or the bot may be launched again after a server restart.
pitfalls.cite: close: You need to delete the webhook before calling this method

pitfalls.text: Returns error 429 in the first 10 minutes after the bot is launched.
pitfalls.cite: close: The method will return error 429 in the first 10 minutes after the bot is launched.

setMyCommands.purpose: Replace the bot's command list for one scope and language.
use_when: publishing the planned menu from the deploy step
a different list per language or per chat
avoid_when: every start with a changing order: send one planned list from deploy

pitfalls.text: At most 100 commands; command is 1-32 lowercase English letters, digits or underscores; description 1-256 characters.
pitfalls.cite: commands: At most 100 commands can be specified.; BotCommand.command: 1-32 characters

pitfalls.text: Only the first list that is set for the user's chat type, scope and language is shown, so a narrower list must repeat the commands users there still need.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#determining-list-of-commands

pitfalls.text: Whether every client shows scoped lists, and how soon after the call, was not tested.

getMyCommands.purpose: Read the command list set for one scope and language.
use_when: verifying after setMyCommands
diffing the live menu against the declared one
avoid_when: working out what a given user sees: it answers for the scope you ask about

pitfalls.text: An unset scope answers with an empty list.
pitfalls.cite: getMyCommands: If commands aren't set, an empty list is returned.

pitfalls.text: Whether an empty answer means a broader scope's list applies to those users is not stated; compare per scope you set.

deleteMyCommands.purpose: Delete the command list of one scope and language so broader lists apply again.
use_when: retiring a per-chat or per-language list
undoing a scope created by mistake
avoid_when: clearing the menu by accident: without scope it targets the default list

pitfalls.text: scope defaults to BotCommandScopeDefault, the list the other scopes end at.
pitfalls.cite: scope: Defaults to BotCommandScopeDefault.

pitfalls.text: Affected users see the higher-level commands afterwards.
pitfalls.cite: deleteMyCommands: After deletion, higher level commands will be shown to affected users.

pitfalls.text: Run it from the planned deploy step, never to tidy up by hand.

setMyName.purpose: Set the bot's display name for all users or for one language.
use_when: per-language names kept in a reviewed profile file
avoid_when: a temporary or test name: users see it in the chat list and profile

pitfalls.text: name is 0-64 characters; an empty string removes the dedicated name for that language.
pitfalls.cite: name: New bot name; 0-64 characters. Pass an empty string to remove the dedicated name

pitfalls.text: An empty language_code is the name for all users whose language has no dedicated name.
pitfalls.cite: language_code: If empty, the name will be shown to all users for whose language there is no dedicated name.

getMyName.purpose: Read the bot's name for one user language.
use_when: checking a per-language name after setMyName

pitfalls.text: language_code is two letters (ISO 639-1) or an empty string.
pitfalls.cite: language_code: A two-letter ISO 639-1 language code or an empty string

pitfalls.text: What it returns for a language without a dedicated name is not stated.

setMyDescription.purpose: Set the text shown in an empty chat with the bot, for all users or for one language.
use_when: the first thing a new user reads: value in one sentence, how to start in the next
avoid_when: the short text on the profile and in shared links: that is setMyShortDescription

pitfalls.text: description is 0-512 characters; an empty string removes the dedicated description for that language.
pitfalls.cite: description: New bot description; 0-512 characters.

pitfalls.text: It is shown only while the chat is empty.
pitfalls.cite: setMyDescription: shown in the chat with the bot if the chat is empty

pitfalls.text: Set it once per deploy and per language, not inside the /start handler.

getMyDescription.purpose: Read the bot's empty-chat description for one user language.
use_when: checking a per-language description after setMyDescription

pitfalls.text: language_code is two letters (ISO 639-1) or an empty string.
pitfalls.cite: language_code: A two-letter ISO 639-1 language code or an empty string

pitfalls.text: What it returns for a language without a dedicated description is not stated.

setMyShortDescription.purpose: Set the short text on the bot's profile page and in shared links, for all users or for one language.
use_when: the one-line promise people see before they open the chat
avoid_when: the empty-chat text: that is setMyDescription

pitfalls.text: short_description is 0-120 characters; an empty string removes the dedicated one for that language.
pitfalls.cite: short_description: New short description for the bot; 0-120 characters.

pitfalls.text: It is sent together with the link when users share the bot.
pitfalls.cite: setMyShortDescription: shown on the bot's profile page and is sent together with the link when users share the bot

getMyShortDescription.purpose: Read the bot's short description for one user language.
use_when: checking a per-language short description after setMyShortDescription

pitfalls.text: language_code is two letters (ISO 639-1) or an empty string.
pitfalls.cite: language_code: A two-letter ISO 639-1 language code or an empty string

pitfalls.text: What it returns for a language without a dedicated short description is not stated.

setChatMenuButton.purpose: Set the menu button of one private chat, or the bot's default menu button.
use_when: opening a Mini App from the menu button (MenuButtonWebApp)
restoring the command list (MenuButtonCommands)
avoid_when: filling the command list: setMyCommands does that

pitfalls.text: Without chat_id it changes the default menu button; with it, one private chat's.
pitfalls.cite: chat_id: If not specified, the bot's default menu button will be changed.

pitfalls.text: A chat's own button other than MenuButtonDefault wins; otherwise the default applies, and by default the button opens the command list.
pitfalls.cite: MenuButton: By default, the menu button opens the list of bot commands.

pitfalls.text: Pick one per bot: Mini App launcher or command list; a Mini App bot keeps /start and /help as commands.

getChatMenuButton.purpose: Read the menu button of one private chat, or the bot's default menu button.
use_when: verifying the button after setChatMenuButton

pitfalls.text: Without chat_id it returns the default menu button.
pitfalls.cite: chat_id: If not specified, the bot's default menu button will be returned.

pitfalls.text: Returns a MenuButton, one of MenuButtonCommands, MenuButtonWebApp or MenuButtonDefault; branch on its type.
pitfalls.cite: getChatMenuButton: Returns MenuButton on success.

setMyDefaultAdministratorRights.purpose: Set the administrator rights suggested when a user adds the bot to a group, supergroup or channel.
use_when: a moderation or posting bot that should be added with the right rights in one step
avoid_when: changing an existing admin's rights: that is promoteChatMember

pitfalls.text: The rights are only suggested; users may change the list before adding the bot.
pitfalls.cite: setMyDefaultAdministratorRights: they are free to modify the list before adding the bot

pitfalls.text: for_channels true sets the channel defaults, otherwise groups and supergroups; omitting rights clears them.
pitfalls.cite: for_channels: Pass True to change the default administrator rights of the bot in channels.

pitfalls.text: Request the minimum and check the granted rights at runtime.

getMyDefaultAdministratorRights.purpose: Read the administrator rights the bot suggests when added to groups, supergroups or channels.
use_when: verifying the defaults after setMyDefaultAdministratorRights

pitfalls.text: for_channels true reads the channel defaults, otherwise groups and supergroups.
pitfalls.cite: for_channels: Pass True to get default administrator rights of the bot in channels.

pitfalls.text: These are the suggestion, not the rights the bot holds in a chat; read those with getChatMember.

setMySettings.purpose: Change the bot's switches (inline mode, privacy mode, groups, topics, callback query mode); unspecified settings stay unchanged.
use_when: the switches live in code and are applied at start-up or deploy
avoid_when: widening what the bot receives (privacy, location, bots) without a human yes

pitfalls.text: can_read_all_group_messages true turns privacy mode OFF.
pitfalls.cite: can_read_all_group_messages: Pass True to disable privacy mode for the bot or False to enable it

pitfalls.text: inline_feedback_share_denominator must be 1, 10, 100 or 1000; 0 stops chosen inline results.
pitfalls.cite: inline_feedback_share_denominator: Must be one of 1, 10, 100, or 1000. Pass 0 to stop receiving chosen inline results.

pitfalls.text: callback_query_mode is default, auto or inline; in auto and inline a callback can arrive with inline_message_id instead of message.
pitfalls.cite: callback_query_mode: Must be one of default, auto, or inline

setMyProfilePhoto.purpose: Set the bot's profile photo from a new static (.JPG) or animated (MPEG4) upload.
use_when: applying a brand avatar kept in the repository

pitfalls.text: The photo can only be a new upload (no file_id, no URL), referenced as attach://<name> from multipart/form-data.
pitfalls.cite: InputProfilePhotoStatic.photo: Profile photos can't be reused and can only be uploaded as a new file

pitfalls.text: photo is InputProfilePhoto: type static (.JPG) or animated (MPEG4, optional main_frame_timestamp for the still).
pitfalls.cite: InputProfilePhoto: InputProfilePhotoStatic, InputProfilePhotoAnimated

use_when: resetting the bot to no photo before a rebrand
avoid_when: replacing the photo: setMyProfilePhoto alone does it

pitfalls.text: Takes no parameters.
pitfalls.cite: removeMyProfilePhoto: Requires no parameters.

pitfalls.text: Keep the source image in the repository so the photo can be set again.

answerCallbackQuery.purpose: Answer a button tap from an inline keyboard or rich message: stop the client's progress bar, optionally with a toast, alert or URL.
use_when: every callback_query, before slow work
a short confirmation or refusal for the presser
avoid_when: results longer than the 200-character text: edit the message or send a new one

pitfalls.text: Clients show a progress bar until it is answered, so answer even when there is nothing to say.
pitfalls.cite: CallbackQuery: it is, therefore, necessary to react by calling answerCallbackQuery even if no notification to the user is needed

pitfalls.text: text is 0-200 characters and nothing is shown without it; show_alert true shows an alert instead of a notification.
pitfalls.cite: text: If not specified, nothing will be shown to the user, 0-200 characters.

pitfalls.text: An ephemeral reply to the query doesn't replace the answer.
pitfalls.cite: EphemeralMessageParameters.callback_query_id: The bot must still answer the callback query using answerCallbackQuery.

pitfalls.text: Answer first, then do the work; keep cache_time at 0 for state-dependent buttons.

savePreparedKeyboardButton.purpose: Store a request_users, request_chat or request_managed_bot button that a Mini App can trigger for a user.
use_when: a Mini App needs the user to pick users, a chat or a managed bot
avoid_when: a button shown in the chat: put it in a reply keyboard instead

pitfalls.text: The button must be of type request_users, request_chat or request_managed_bot.
pitfalls.cite: button: The button must be of the type request_users, request_chat, or request_managed_bot.

pitfalls.text: Inside the Mini App call WebApp.requestChat(id) with the returned id; where the pick arrives is not stated (in a reply keyboard it is users_shared / chat_shared).
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/webapps#initializing-mini-apps (requestChat: id of a PreparedKeyboardButton from savePreparedKeyboardButton)
